full_text_en:
Beijing International Trust and Investment Company v. Beijing Korean-Russian Style Restaurant Co., Ltd. and North China Electric Power Complete Equipment Company — dispute over a loan contract (appeal)

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): North China Electric Power Equipment Complete Company.

Legal Representative: Zhang Chunyuan, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Yeli, Vice General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Shi Jianying, Legal Counsel of the Company.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Beijing International Trust and Investment Company.

Legal Representative: Zhang Honghai, General Manager.

Agents ad litem: Zhang Yuming and Chen Jinzhan, lawyers of Tongshang Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Beijing Korean-Russian Style Restaurant Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Bai Yongqing, General Manager.

The Appellant, North China Electric Power Equipment Complete Company (hereinafter referred to as NCPC), appealed against the civil judgment of first instance rendered by the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court to the Beijing High People's Court in the case of dispute over a loan contract with the Appellees, Beijing International Trust and Investment Company (hereinafter referred to as BITIC) and Beijing Korean-Russian Style Restaurant Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Korean-Russian Style Restaurant).

The Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court found that: The entrusted loan agreement entered into between BITIC and Korean-Russian Style Restaurant was in essence a loan contract, and therefore the agreement between the parties regarding service fees was clearly in violation of national laws and regulations and should be held invalid; the agreement regarding fines was clearly excessive and should be implemented at the standard set by the People's Bank of China for the same period. Since the main terms of the contract did not violate legal provisions, the contract should be held valid. NCPC, as the guarantor, failed to provide relevant evidence that it should not bear the guaranty liability after issuing the guarantee letter, and therefore could not be relieved of its guaranty liability. NCPC's defense could not be established. Accordingly, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. The loan contract entered into between the parties was valid except for the service fee clause, which was invalid, and the guaranty provided by NCPC was also valid; 2. Within ten days after this judgment takes effect, Korean-Russian Style Restaurant shall pay BITIC RMB 3,000,000, together with interest and penalty interest thereon; 3. NCPC shall bear the liability for compensation for the above amount; 4. BITIC's other claims are dismissed.

NCPC appealed, arguing that: The first instance court's finding that a guaranty relationship existed lacked factual and legal basis and was clearly erroneous. The Appellant never issued a guarantee letter to BITIC. The "guarantee letter" was the result of malicious collusion between the Plaintiff, BITIC, and the Defendant, Korean-Russian Style Restaurant, who rearranged and repurposed the guarantee letter that the Appellant intended to provide for Beijing Ocean Electronics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ocean Electronics) for BITIC's benefit. The original judgment's view that, merely because there was a company seal, the guaranty relationship was valid regardless of whether the Appellant knew or consented to it, is one-sided. The Appellant requests the revocation of the original judgment and a new judgment in accordance with the law.

BITIC submitted to the first instance judgment; Korean-Russian Style Restaurant did not appear in court for either the first or second instance trial.

The Beijing High People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

On November 10, 1993, the Securities Department of BITIC and Korean-Russian Style Restaurant entered into Entrusted Loan Agreement No. BM93-44 (standard form contract), stipulating that: BITIC would provide a loan of RMB 3,000,000 to Korean-Russian Style Restaurant, with an annual interest rate of 10.8%, and a loan service fee of 0.9%. The loan term was from November 10, 1993, to February 10, 1994. If Korean-Russian Style Restaurant failed to repay the loan principal and interest on time, a daily penalty interest of 0.5% would be charged. The guarantee clause of the contract stated that this loan was guaranteed by an unconditional and irrevocable guarantee letter issued by NCPC. If the borrower failed to repay on time, the guarantor was jointly and severally liable for the loan principal, interest, penalty interest, and all related expenses. The original contract was in three copies, with one copy each for the trustee (BITIC), the borrower, and the guarantor. Korean-Russian Style Restaurant signed and affixed its seal in the borrower column and indicated its bank and account number; in the trustee column, besides the seal of the Securities Department of BITIC, the entries for legal representative, bank, and account number were left blank; in the guarantor column, NCPC did not sign or affix its seal. Korean-Russian Style Restaurant provided BITIC with a guarantee letter undated and bearing the seal of NCPC. The guarantee letter stated: On the request of Korean-Russian Style Restaurant, NCPC, based on the contract No. BM93-44 signed between BITIC and Korean-Russian Style Restaurant on November 1 (should be November 10), 1993, is willing to provide an irrevocable guarantee letter for this loan, with a guaranteed amount of RMB 3,000,000, and a guarantee period (handwritten) "valid until January 15, 1994." This guarantee letter took effect upon signature and seal, and its validity period extended until the borrower had repaid all outstanding loan principal, interest, penalty interest, and all expenses. The guarantee letter bore the seal of NCPC, the signature of "Zhang Chunyuan," and indicated the guarantor's bank as Bank of China, Beijing Branch, and account number 019461022. The specific date of the guarantee letter was left blank.

After the contract was concluded, BITIC, without verifying the guarantee with NCPC, transferred RMB 3,000,000 to Korean-Russian Style Restaurant on November 13, 1993. Upon the maturity of the loan, Korean-Russian Style Restaurant failed to repay the loan principal and interest as agreed. BITIC repeatedly demanded repayment from the borrower, and Korean-Russian Style Restaurant promised to extend the repayment on three separate occasions: July 25, 1995, October 30, 1995, and January 31, 1996, but none of these promises were fulfilled. BITIC never sought recourse against NCPC for the above amount. NCPC only learned of this guarantee upon the first instance litigation.

It was also found that Bai Yongqing, the legal representative of Korean-Russian Style Restaurant, was also the chairman of Ocean Electronics. In the summer of 1993, NCPC had business dealings with Bai Yongqing of Ocean Electronics regarding plywood. NCPC intended to provide a loan guarantee for Ocean Electronics, but due to failure to agree on a counter-guarantee (Ocean Electronics offered the then-unregistered Korean-Russian Style Restaurant as a counter-guarantee, which NCPC did not accept), NCPC returned the blank "guarantee letter" bearing NCPC's seal and the handwritten phrase "valid until January 15, 1994" to Ocean Electronics. This letter was subsequently altered by Bai Yongqing and used as a guarantee for the loan from BITIC to Korean-Russian Style Restaurant. The photocopy of the "guarantee letter" provided by BITIC to the first instance court at the time of filing the lawsuit was inconsistent with the original submitted later; the original contained a handwritten guarantee period, while the photocopy did not. Upon forensic examination, the signature of the legal representative on the "guarantee letter" was not written by Zhang Chunyuan himself. The parties confirmed that the bank and account number indicated for the guarantor on the "guarantee letter" belonged to BITIC itself, not to NCPC.

The above facts are confirmed by the evidence on file, including: the loan contract between BITIC and Korean-Russian Style Restaurant, the guarantee letter, the loan disbursement voucher, Korean-Russian Style Restaurant's three written promises to extend repayment; the power of attorney between NCPC and Ocean Electronics concerning the plywood business, the receipt issued by Ocean Electronics after returning the "guarantee letter," and the statements of the parties.

The Beijing High People's Court held that: The first instance court's determination of the nature and validity of the contract between BITIC and Korean-Russian Style Restaurant, as well as its judgment ordering Korean-Russian Style Restaurant to pay BITIC RMB 3,000,000 and interest, was legally grounded and should be affirmed. However, the first instance court's determination that the guarantee by NCPC was valid and its order that NCPC bear compensation liability lacked factual and legal basis. This guarantee did not represent NCPC's true intention. NCPC had never received a request for a guarantee from Korean-Russian Style Restaurant, nor had it issued a guarantee letter to BITIC for this loan. Although the seal of NCPC appeared on the guarantee letter in question, it was not affixed for the purpose of guaranteeing this loan but for a loan guarantee intended for Ocean Electronics. Moreover, the signature of the legal representative, Zhang Chunyuan, was forged. More notably, the bank and account number of the guarantor on the guarantee letter belonged to the creditor, BITIC, not to NCPC; the handwritten validity period of the guarantee letter until January 15, 1994, was earlier than the maturity date of the main contract, which was unreasonable, and by the time the loan term of the main contract expired on February 10, 1994, the guarantee had already lapsed. Even if this "guarantee letter" were valid, BITIC, after the loan contract term had expired and without the consent of the guarantor NCPC, agreed to extend the repayment three times with Korean-Russian Style Restaurant. Pursuant to the Supreme People's Court's "Reply on Whether the Guarantor Continues to Bear Guaranty Liability after the Parties to a Loan Contract Reach an Agreement on Extending the Repayment Period without the Guarantor's Consent," NCPC's guaranty liability should also be discharged.

In summary, the guarantee contract relationship involved in this case, whether viewed from the perspective of the parties' expressions of intent, the form of the guarantee, or the content of the guarantee agreement, was not genuine and contravened China's guarantee legal system. Therefore, the guarantee should be held invalid. NCPC should not bear compensation liability for this loan. Its grounds of appeal are established and are supported by this Court. The first instance judgment was partially erroneous in fact-finding and application of law, and should be corrected. Accordingly, the Beijing High People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on January 27, 1999:

1. Items 2 and 4 of the civil judgment (No. (1997) Er Zhong Jing Chu Zi No. 301) of the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court are affirmed (i.e., within ten days after this judgment takes effect, Korean-Russian Style Restaurant shall pay BITIC RMB 3,000,000, together with interest and penalty interest thereon; BITIC's other claims are dismissed);

2. Item 1 of the original judgment is modified as follows: The loan contract between BITIC and Korean-Russian Style Restaurant is valid except for the service fee clause, which is invalid; the guarantee contract is invalid, and NCPC shall not bear guaranty liability;

3. Item 3 of the original judgment (i.e., NCPC shall bear compensation liability for the above repayment) is reversed.

Court acceptance fee for first instance: RMB 33,169, of which BITIC shall bear RMB 3,169, and Korean-Russian Style Restaurant shall bear RMB 30,000.

Court acceptance fee for second instance: RMB 33,169, of which the appellees BITIC and Korean-Russian Style Restaurant shall each bear RMB 16,584.5.
